title: Nvidia's Proposed $5B Credit Guarantee for Nscale Would Grant Chipmaker Title to Facility on Default
summary:
Nvidia is negotiating a specific financing structure that would allow it to take ownership of a data center if its partner, Nscale, defaults on its debt. The proposed "residual value" guarantee for the 460MW West Virginia campus would mean the chipmaker takes physical title to the facility and becomes the direct landlord for AI developer Anthropic should the cloud provider fail to meet its loan obligations, The Information reported.

The credit support, estimated to be over $5B, is intended to cover construction and power costs for a project tied to a $45B compute contract between Nscale and Anthropic. The facility is expected to use Nvidia's next-generation Vera Rubin GPUs. A final agreement has not yet been signed; meanwhile, Nscale disclosed in September that it had no binding financing commitments for the project and reported a net loss of $1.02B against $140.6M in first-half revenue.

$NVDA is in talks to provide Nscale with billions of dollars in credit guarantees to finance a 460MW data center in West Virginia for Anthropic.

Nscale has a $45B contract with Anthropic for the facility, which is expected to use NVIDIA's Vera Rubin GPUs.

The credit support could exceed $5B, based on industry estimates, and would cover power and construction costs rather than chip purchases.

The agreement has not yet been signed, and terms could change.

Source: The Information
